workflow-run-steps-rely-on-bash-defaults.search: Run steps in the Copilot agent GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml) inherit defaults.run.shell set to bash, which GitHub runs with -e and -o pipefail. A failed gh api command substitution or a failing jq pipeline therefore already fails the step, so adding an explicit set -euo pipefail inside run blocks is redundant. This only holds while the shell stays bash; a step that overrides the shell needs its own error handling.

Both currently cover .github/workflows and .github/actions yml files, and changing only one leaves Claude and Copilot with different scopes. Widening the glob to composite actions also applies workflow-only sections such as runs-on, defaults.run.shell and setup-* wrapper advice to composite actions, which reviewers objected to.

The pinned actions/cache v6.1.0 ignores ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE, so the Hugging Face cache restore action in .github/actions/cache-hf logs an expected cache write denied warning on each read run.

a-hanging-server-info-request-leaves-the.search: Server-info fetch that gates the MLflow UI router in the experiment-tracking frontend (useServerInfo hook, fetchServerInfo) is the chokepoint for whether the app renders at all. Requests such as opening MLflow behind a slow or proxied server, where the page stays on a loading skeleton, go through this request. The rule is to bound the request with an AbortController plus setTimeout using SERVER_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS, pass controller.signal into fetchAPI, clear the timer in finally, and treat AbortError in the catch as a DEFAULT_RESPONSE fallback with a console.warn. Use AbortController rather than AbortSignal.timeout because older Chrome versions lack it, and keep the bound around 30s.

empty-upstream-error-bodies-must-fall-ba.search: Error bodies returned by upstream model providers are parsed in mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py (_error_detail, send_stream_request, send_proxy_request) and turned into the HTTP exception detail shown to gateway users. Empty or unreadable provider error bodies must fall back to the aiohttp reason phrase e.message, because response.json() returns None and response.text() returns an empty string for empty bodies. enable-gh-api-request-logging-in-bot-wor.search: Diagnostic logging for the gh CLI inside GitHub Actions bot steps in .github/workflows/update-model-catalog.yml and .github/workflows/uv.yml, where the GH_DEBUG=api environment variable is set on the step that runs gh pr create or the pr step to log HTTP requests. environment-provenance-is-merged-into-tr.search: The TypeScript SDK span processors in libs/typescript/core/src/exporters, MlflowSpanProcessor in mlflow.ts and DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor in uc_table.ts, build trace metadata in onStart. every-actions-create-github-app-token-st.search: GitHub Actions workflows and composite actions in this repository that mint GitHub App installation tokens with actions/create-github-app-token are checked by the conftest policy in .github/policy.rego, rule deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope. every-crewai-autolog-span-write-must-go-.search: CrewAI autologging in mlflow/crewai/autolog.py writes span attributes and inputs for Agents, Tasks, Crews and LLM calls. The _get_agent_attributes, _get_task_attributes and _get_llm_attributes helpers apply the same key filter, and _get_llm_attributes skips callbacks. every-experiment-page-sub-route-needs-an.search: The MLflow experiment page in mlflow/server/js/src/experiment-tracking/components/experiment-page routes sub-pages to side navigation tabs through the ExperimentPageRoutePathToTabNameMap in useGetExperimentPageActiveTabByRoute.tsx. bedrock-anthropic-passthrough-only-anthr.search: Claude models on AWS Bedrock reached through the gateway's Anthropic passthrough path are handled by AmazonBedrockProvider._passthrough in mlflow/gateway/providers/bedrock.py, covering requests on the messages route and the endpoint credential setup for Bedrock. The passthrough accepts only Anthropic models (AmazonBedrockModelProvider.ANTHROPIC, otherwise 400) and only bearer-token auth (self._is_token_auth, otherwise 501). Client auth headers are removed by _drop_client_auth_headers in providers/base.py before the endpoint's Bedrock token headers from _get_token_auth_headers are merged, so the client's own key, including a credential agent's key, never reaches Bedrock. A gateway endpoint configured with an IAM role or access key (SigV4) gets a 501 from this passthrough, which is intentional because SigV4 invoke_model support was left out of that change.

Make sure a client's Authorization header is never forwarded to AWS Bedrock when using the Anthropic passthrough.

bedrock-streaming-exception-frames-must-.search: Streaming Claude responses served from AWS Bedrock through the gateway are converted from Bedrock event-stream frames into Anthropic-style server-sent events by _event_stream_to_anthropic_sse in mlflow/gateway/providers/bedrock.py. Non-event frames such as throttling, service unavailable and model timeout exceptions are mapped to HTTP status via _BEDROCK_STREAM_EXCEPTION_STATUS (ThrottlingException 429, service unavailable 503, modelTimeoutException 408), with any other exception frame defaulting to 502. The mapped status is raised as HTTPException so safe_stream writes that status into the SSE error chunk, the same way pre-stream errors are reported by send_stream_request. Without this, a stream that fails after it started shows only a generic error, and the client cannot tell throttling from unavailability or a timeout.
says: Streaming Claude on Bedrock through the gateway shows a generic error when the model is throttled mid-response; show the real 429 status instead.
Distinguish throttling, service unavailable and timeout errors in the streamed error event from Bedrock Claude.
Surface the correct status code in the SSE error chunk when a Bedrock stream fails after it started.

boolean-column-predicates-must-use-true-.search: Tracking-store queries that filter boolean columns in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py run on SQLAlchemy against any configured backend, including Microsoft SQL Server. The default label schema lookup in _ensure_default_label_schema filtered SqlLabelSchema.is_default with .is_(True), which compiles to IS 1 and fails on MSSQL 2022 and older. Boolean predicates should be written as equality with sqlalchemy.true(), which compiles to = 1 on MSSQL and is valid elsewhere. Only that one call site was changed, so other .is_(True) filters on boolean columns need auditing before they are assumed safe on SQL Server.
says: Label schema questions fail to load when MLflow uses SQL Server 2022 as the tracking backend.

bot-pr-creation-and-reuse-paths-must-app.search: Automated pull requests created or reused by Dependabot, the uv.lock sync workflow, and the model catalog update workflow in the repository's .github directory are eligible for CI auto-retry only when they carry the auto-rerun label at the time the retry sweep runs. Each bot-PR path must add that label both when it creates a PR (gh pr create --label or gh pr edit --add-label in uv.yml and update-model-catalog.yml, plus the labels list in .github/dependabot.yml) and when it reuses an existing PR. On uv.yml the create path adds the label after the existing sleep 5, while the reuse path adds it without that delay. Bot PRs that are only labeled on creation are left out of automatic reruns of failed CI, so they stay unretried after failures. Human-opened PRs need the label applied by hand.

bounded-retry-for-pypi-release-date-fetc.search: The dev script dev/remove_experimental_decorators.py fetches MLflow release dates from PyPI through get_mlflow_release_dates, which is used when cleaning up experimental decorators in CI. The fetch now makes up to 3 urlopen attempts with timeout=10, retrying on URLError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError and HTTPError codes 429 or 5xx, with sleep 2**attempt between tries and the last failure re-raised. Other HTTP errors are re-raised immediately, and the HTTPError handler must come before the URLError handler because HTTPError is a subclass of URLError. JSON is parsed only after the loop. Before this change a single unbounded request meant one transient reset aborted the CI job.

branch-2-13-package-builds-go-through-de.search: Release packaging for the branch-2.13 release line is handled by dev/build.sh, while dev/build.py is only a shim. The python.yml release workflow calls dev/build.py:main with --package-type release or skinny, and the shim runs bash dev/build.sh, adding --skinny for skinny. mlflow is built from pyproject.toml and mlflow-skinny from pyproject.skinny.toml. Changes to how 2.13 packages are built belong in dev/build.sh, not in the shim, and dev/build.py is dev and CI only, not shipped in the mlflow or mlflow-skinny wheels. This applies only to the 2.13 branch; v3+ branches have their own build.py logic.

budget-amount-is-deliberately-not-part-o.search: Budget enforcement in the Redis budget tracker in mlflow/gateway/budget_tracker/redis.py decides whether a gateway request is rejected based on a budget window's cumulative spend. A window's identity is its bounds plus the duration fields that produced them, so _ENSURE_WINDOW_LUA compares window_start, duration_unit and duration_value only, and RedisBudgetTracker.should_reject_request uses _window_duration_matches on those duration fields. budget_amount is deliberately excluded, so editing only the spending cap keeps the existing window and its cumulative_spend and applies the new limit to it. Adding the amount to the compared or stored fields would roll the window on every cap edit and discard accumulated spend, while duration edits must still roll the window.
says: Editing the budget limit should not reset the spend already recorded for a gateway budget.

fractional-model-version-literals-must-b.search: Model-version search filters in the SQL model-registry store, where a version_number value in a filter such as version_number = 1.5 is parsed and coerced to an integer in SQLAlchemyStore._get_search_model_versions_filter_clauses. Unquoted decimal literals arrive as Python floats, and the guard must reject them with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE before int() runs. Quoted strings like version_number='2' still pass. The FileStore matcher SearchModelVersionUtils._does_model_version_match_clauses still calls int() and can truncate, so backends may disagree.

fractional-numeric-filter-values-must-be.search: Numeric attribute filters for runs, registered models and logged models are matched in memory by SearchUtils._does_run_match_clause, _does_model_match_clause and _does_logged_model_match_clause in mlflow/utils/search_utils.py. Fractional values such as start_time = 1.5 must stay exact floats, so the matchers only convert value when it is a string and never call int() on an already-parsed float. The SQL run path passes the float to SQLAlchemy as FLOAT, so both paths must agree. Experiments and evaluation datasets are excluded and must reject fractions instead.

fs2db-migration-is-sqlite-only-so-postgr.search: The filestore-to-database migration under mlflow/store/fs2db, run by the migrate-filestore CLI, only accepts SQLite targets: cli.py rejects every non-SQLite database URL, and migrate() in mlflow/store/fs2db/__init__.py registers a SQLite-only PRAGMA listener on the engine. Requests to migrate a file-based tracking store to PostgreSQL or another database through this path cannot reach a PostgreSQL engine. PostgreSQL driver URL normalization therefore does not belong in this module.

gateway-auth-config-delivered-list-optio.search: AI Gateway endpoint configuration for database-managed endpoints, where provider settings are delivered through auth_config, a map of string values, and copied by _build_endpoint_config in mlflow/server/gateway_api.py. The validate_vertex_anthropic_betas before-validator in mlflow/gateway/config.py splits on commas, strips whitespace and drops empties, and returns non-string values unchanged for YAML configs. gateway-authz-validators-must-read-resou.search: Authorization validators for AI Gateway resources (secrets, model definitions, endpoints, guardrail and binding routes) in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py. Validators must parse the request with _get_request_message into the proto and use msg.<field> for the resource ID, because _get_request_param('secret_id') reads only raw keys and misses camelCase JSON-name aliases such as secretId. The result is that permission is checked against a different secret or endpoint than the handler acts on, which can allow a secret update or delete to hit the wrong resource. Shared helpers such as _get_gateway_secret_permission take an explicit ID, and a GET by name first resolves endpoint_id through the tracking store.

gateway-list-routes-need-authentication-.search: Listing AI Gateway endpoints through the models discovery route GET /gateway/mlflow/v1/models when authentication is enabled. _get_gateway_validator maps that route to the authentication-only validator, and the per-endpoint filter _filter_list_gateway_models, registered in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS for list_models, drops each item the caller lacks USE permission on via _validate_gateway_use_permission. Administrators keep access through the same helper.

every-openai-autolog-streaming-span-must.search: Streaming responses from the OpenAI integration, including chat completions and the Responses API, are instrumented by the OpenAI autolog wrapper in mlflow/openai/autolog.py. _stream_output_logging_hook wraps the stream for both sync and async callers, and the span is ended through _process_last_chunk on normal completion and _end_span_on_exception when the stream raises. Every span started for a streamed OpenAI call must be ended once the stream stops yielding, whether it completes or fails; if this is skipped, the span stays open and the trace for that call is never exported until it times out. Early consumer stops such as break or close() are not covered by this invariant.

every-public-review-queues-function-need.search: Public functions in the review queues SDK in mlflow/genai/review_queues/__init__.py are blocked on Databricks tracking URIs by the @databricks_api_disabled decorator, which embeds the function's exact __name__ in an INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE error that points users to the workspace Reviews UI. Adding or renaming a review queue function requires the decorator's first argument to match the function name and a matching entry in the parametrized test_databricks_tracking_uri_rejected list in tests/genai/review_queues/test_review_queues_sdk.py, using the _REVIEWS_UI_ALTERNATIVE message constant. Without the guard, the call reaches the OSS /api/3.0/mlflow/review-queues routes on Databricks and fails with a misleading INTERNAL_ERROR Not Found.

example-tests-must-reuse-the-shared-pre-.search: Example tests under tests/examples that call MLflow tracking APIs, such as test_typesafe_judges_example in tests/examples/test_examples.py, should reuse the shared pre-migrated db_uri fixture instead of creating a fresh SQLite file under tmp_path. Creating a new database made every run reapply all migrations, which is why the example suite is slow in CI, especially on Windows. The fix pattern is to take db_uri as an argument, call mlflow.set_tracking_uri(db_uri), restore the previous URI with request.addfinalizer, and drop the tmp_path argument; tests that must exercise migrations or an empty database should not use this shortcut.

experiment-and-evaluation-dataset-numeri.search: Experiment and evaluation dataset search filters in the SQLAlchemy tracking store, handled by _get_search_experiments_filter_clauses and _get_search_datasets_filter_clauses in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py, accept only integer numeric values, such as timestamp comparisons in those searches. The shared SearchUtils._get_value parser now returns floats for fractional literals, so the isinstance(value, float) check must run before int() coercion and raise INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. Without that check, fractional timestamps are silently truncated in SQL and the search returns matches that should not exist; run and MCP searches intentionally keep float comparisons and must not get this guard.

extras-defined-in-dev-pyproject-py-must-.search: Optional dependency extras of the mlflow package, such as the db extra used for PostgreSQL or MySQL tracking database URLs, are authored in the build function in dev/pyproject.py, which generates the root pyproject.toml, pyproject.release.toml and libs/skinny/pyproject.toml. Changing an extra means editing dev/pyproject.py, rerunning the generator until it produces no diff, then running uv lock and uv lock --check so uv.lock matches; hand-editing generated pyproject files, or relying on a dev-only group in uv.lock, does not change what the published wheel installs. A known failure was the db extra shipping only psycopg2-binary, so a postgresql tracking URL raised ModuleNotFoundError for psycopg; psycopg2-binary should stay alongside psycopg[binary] for older SQLAlchemy versions and explicit psycopg2 URLs.

fastapi-response-filters-are-opted-in-by.search: Response filtering for user-scoped collection results on FastAPI routes under basic-auth is opted in per endpoint function in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py. A route gets a filter only if its endpoint function object is a key in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS, resolved by _find_fastapi_response_filter from request.scope['endpoint'] inside fastapi_permission_middleware; the old GET-only gate was removed, so POST collection routes such as search_jobs in mlflow/server/job_api.py are filtered once registered. The filter applies only to non-admin users with a status code below 400, and if a route is not registered it returns the unfiltered handler result with no error. Flask routes are not covered by this mechanism.

The tests in dev/flavors/tests/test_matrix.py are globally skipped, so no active test asserts the default or the version-specific override, and a change should add an unskipped unit test for both.

flavor-serialization-format-default-is-r.search: The save and log APIs for the sklearn, PyTorch and LightGBM flavors take a serialization_format argument whose default depends on the environment, resolved by each flavor's _get_default_serialization_format when the argument is omitted. On Databricks Runtime or with a databricks tracking URI, the default must match the earlier cloudpickle or pickle output instead of skops for sklearn and LightGBM or pt2 for PyTorch, so the signatures default to None and save_model and log_model resolve it using is_in_databricks_runtime or is_databricks_uri. Hard-coded signature defaults caused models logged on Databricks to switch serializer and change artifacts and dependencies; explicit values still override the default, and PyTorch export_model=True must still resolve to pt2 before the Databricks check.

gateway-secret-create-needs-a-workspace-.search: Gateway secret creation in the basic-auth app (mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py) is authorized by a before-request validator, validate_can_create_gateway_secret, which checks workspace-level create permission through _user_can_create_in_workspace. Create requests such as adding an AI Gateway secret or provider credential pass through _authorized_outside_before_request's fail-closed check, and any create route that also registers an after-request set_can_manage_* ownership grant needs its own before-request validator. The after-request grant only records ownership and does not authorize creation. Symptom: with workspaces enabled, a user denied experiment or registered-model creation could still create a gateway secret.

pass-untrusted-issue-text-into-workflow-.search: GitHub Actions workflows in this repo that react to issues or pull requests, such as the triage workflow in .github/workflows/triage.yml, must pass user-controlled event fields like the issue title or body into a `run:` step through an `env:` variable, then read them as quoted shell variables. payload-only-eligibility-guards-belong-i.search: The community-label GitHub Actions workflow in .github/workflows/community-label.yml decides which pull requests get the community label, and its jobs.label-community.if expression is where cheap event-payload exclusions belong. per-row-permission-predicates-in-graphql.search: The GraphQL authorization middleware GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py applies per-row read predicates such as _rm_or_prompt_read_predicate and the model-version read predicate to list results, for example when the UI lists up to 100 runs in mlflowSearchRuns with nested modelVersions. Each nested resolution rebuilds the predicate, which costs a user lookup and a SQL grants query per row, making the runs table slower. The fix memoizes the predicate per request in GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._model_version_read_predicate using the flask g context keyed by username, shared by top-level and nested paths. The cache is scoped to a single request, so grant changes made during that request are not seen, and it must not be shared across requests.

Cache user grant lookups per request so the runs list doesn't query permissions for every row

pr-paths-ignore-lists-must-mirror-the-we.search: Pull request path filters (paths-ignore) in MLflow GitHub Actions workflows such as master.yml, tracing.yml, examples.yml, cross-version-tests.yml, fs2db.yml, build-wheel.yml, and r.yml decide whether CI runs for a PR. These lists previously excluded only the web JS paths (mlflow/server/js/** and js.yml), so PRs that touch only the TypeScript SDK in libs/typescript or only Copilot workflow files (copilot-*.yml) started unrelated jobs like MLflow tests, tracing, examples, fs2db, build-wheel and R. The fix adds libs/typescript/** and .github/workflows/typescript.yml after the js.yml entry, and adds .github/workflows/copilot-*.yml before docs.yml, in pull_request lists only. Mixed PRs still run because paths-ignore skips a run only when every changed file matches.

The handler's destructured parameters { github, context, core } must match the object literal passed as script({ github, context, core }). protect-workflow-is-rerun-last-and-only-.search: Retry of failed CI workflows for a commit is handled by .github/workflows/retry.sh, which loops over the failed run rows, sends non-protect reruns in the background, and records the protect workflow run in protect_id. The protect run is rerun only after wait returns, so it is requested after the other rerun requests have been sent. Keeping Protect out of the parallel batch avoids the Protect check failing immediately on a retry and using up one of the commit's limited retry attempts while other workflows are still being rerun. Submission should happen only when every preceding rerun request succeeds, and a failure must still give a nonzero exit; backgrounded rerun calls do not report their status, so that check has to be added explicitly. Only one protect run is tracked.

protect-yml-is-detected-by-its-exact-fil.search: The CI retry script .github/workflows/retry.sh identifies the protect workflow by exact filename, protect.yml. The jq filter in the runs variable sets each row's workflow field to the basename of .workflowRun.workflow.resourcePath, and the while read loop stores the protect run as protect_id and protect_workflow. The protect rerun is issued after the wait that follows the loop over the other rows. Comparing the workflow field against a path such as an endswith check on /protect.yml silently never matches, so protect is either rerun as an ordinary parallel job or skipped. protobuf-request-parsers-must-reject-bod.search: Request bodies for proto-backed REST endpoints in MLflow are parsed in mlflow/server/handlers.py by _get_request_message and _get_workspace_request_message through protobuf parse_dict, which accepts both snake_case and camelCase field names and lets the later key win. Gateway secret and other endpoints that authorize on one field can therefore act on a different id if a body spells the same field both ways. _reject_conflicting_field_aliases checks the raw request JSON before parse_dict and returns INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE (400) when a field is spelled both ways, recursing into nested messages and lists; map entries and google.protobuf well-known types are skipped, and a single spelling is accepted. Every request-body parse_dict call in handlers.py must run this check.

provider-free-model-cost-lookup-must-ite.search: Cost calculation for LLM spans in MLflow uses the bundled provider pricing catalogs in mlflow/utils/providers.py, and when a span has a model name but no model_provider, _list_provider_names scans every provider catalog to find the first match. The listing previously came from Path.glob without sorting, whose order depends on the filesystem, so the same model name could get a different cost on Linux than on macOS. The fix wraps the listing in sorted(), and any new listing of bundled catalog files must also be sorted. The fixed order only matters on the provider-free path; when model_provider is passed no cross-provider scan happens. tests/utils/test_providers.py asserts the listing is sorted.

psycopg-v3-regression-tests-go-in-tests-.search: Regression tests for the psycopg v3 numeric and timestamp search filters on the MLflow tracking store and model registry store go in tests/db/test_workspace_tracking_store.py, using the psycopg3_store or psycopg3_registry_store fixtures. These fixtures build their URI through _psycopg3_uri(), which rewrites MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI to postgresql+psycopg, and they skip unless the tracking URI is PostgreSQL and psycopg is importable. Generic store fixtures run on SQLite or psycopg2 and cannot detect the psycopg v3 VARCHAR bind bug, so tests there pass on the old code. pt2-archives-must-be-validated-before-to.search: PyTorch model loading in mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py for pt2 archives saved with serialization_format="pt2" passes through _load_by_pickle_check, which must refuse unsafe archives when MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION is false. Before torch.export.load runs, _validate_pt2_archive_is_pickle_free checks each record: text and JSON metadata and raw tensor records marked use_pickle false pass, while every other record must load under torch.load with weights_only=True, otherwise an MlflowException names the record. _pickle_globals statically scans data.pkl with pickletools to reject user-registered globals, and the check fails closed on unparseable streams. pt2 is refused on torch versions below 2.10, and the check is skipped in Databricks Runtime and Model Serving through _is_pickle_deserialization_allowed. Without this guard a crafted pt2 archive can run code during load, or a model loads with no clear reason when pickle is disabled.

promote-latest-must-stay-in-its-own-fixe.search: Docker image publishing in the push-images GitHub Actions workflow: the promote-latest job moves the floating latest image tags to a release, and it runs only when the check-latest job decides the release is the newest one. The rule is that promote-latest keeps its own fixed concurrency group (push-images-promote-latest, cancel-in-progress false), the check-latest decision stays in its own job, and neither push-images nor check-latest gets a concurrency block. The Latest re-check inside promote-latest must still run before the imagetools create writes. A non-latest release run can replace a pending canonical promotion in the shared group and then skip, so the canonical release never gets its latest docker tag.

prompt-cache-entries-must-be-scoped-by-r.search: Prompt loading in the MLflow prompt registry: load_prompt and the MlflowClient prompt methods read and invalidate a process-wide PromptCache in mlflow/prompt/registry_utils.py, keyed by PromptCacheKey and cleared through PromptCache.delete_all. Cache keys must include a registry namespace (a sha256 of the resolved registry URI, built in _get_prompt_cache_namespace) and the active workspace, with registry_uri a required keyword on from_parts, from_uri, delete and delete_all, and the raw URI never placed in the key because it can hold credentials. Bulk invalidation must use the same from_parts path so its scope matches the keys. When one process uses two registries or workspaces, load_prompt can return another registry's or workspace's prompt version without contacting the registry it was asked for, until the TTL expires.

prompt-code-path-is-selected-only-by-an-.search: Model registry create path in the MLflow server: the CreateModelVersion request handler in mlflow/server/handlers.py decides whether a new model version is a prompt or a regular model version from the mlflow.prompt.is_prompt request tag, through _is_prompt_request. Only an effective value of "true" (case-insensitive) selects the prompt branch, with duplicate tag keys resolved last-wins the same way ModelVersion._is_prompt resolves them. Both branches must agree with the entity-level prompt check. If a tag value such as "false" selects the prompt branch, a regular model version skips source run and source model validation, and a duplicate-tag pair can take the prompt path for an entity that is not a prompt.

prompt-placeholder-source-strings-are-a-.search: Prompt creation sources in MLflow: the Python client's register_prompt, the store's create_prompt_version, and the prompt creation form in the web UI all create prompt model versions with a placeholder source string. The UI literal in mlflow/server/js/src/experiment-tracking/pages/prompts/api.ts is not imported and has to be edited by hand, and any new sender must add its placeholder to the allowlist. promptversion-must-not-write-its-interna.search: Prompt version construction in MLflow entities: PromptVersion.__init__ in mlflow/entities/model_registry/prompt_version.py takes a caller-supplied tags dict and adds internal keys to it (mlflow.prompt.text, mlflow.prompt.type, mlflow.prompt.is_prompt, and the model config). The original code aliased the caller's dict with tags or {}, so the fix is to copy it first with dict(tags or {}), and the same copy-before-write pattern applies to any entity constructor that adds keys to a passed dict. Reusing one tags dict for two prompt versions makes the second prompt carry the first prompt's model config and template tags, and the caller's dict gains mlflow.prompt.* keys. The copy is shallow, so nested values remain shared.

My tags dictionary gets mlflow.prompt keys added after I create a prompt version.

protect-empty-workflow-run-discovery-mus.search: The Protect pull request gate in .github/workflows/protect.js: its workflow-run discovery step lists runs for the PR head SHA with listWorkflowRunsForRepo and filters out protect.yml itself, event dynamic, and IGNORED_WORKFLOWS. The fix re-runs that same paginated listing and filters up to 3 times, sleeping 5000 ms and logging core.warning per empty attempt, and then throws an error asking for a job rerun, so an empty response fails closed. The latest-rerun dedup and failure detection are unchanged, and a PR whose SHA truly has no expected workflow runs also fails after about 10 seconds. The throw conflicts with an existing core.setFailed expectation for protect failures, and that conflict is flagged rather than resolved. Without the retry, Protect can report success on the DCO check alone while the MLflow workflow tests are still running.

protect-js-check-log-order-is-the-key-or.search: Check output ordering in the Protect workflow script .github/workflows/protect.js: checks are sorted by STATUS_ORDER, which is Object.values of the STATE object, right before the console print loop. Reordering STATE keys changes printed priority, which is currently failure, pending, success, then skipped. A status string that is not a STATE key gets indexOf -1 and sorts above every known status, so it appears at the top of the log. A new status should be added to STATE at the position where it should be prioritised, not only pushed as a string at a check site.

A new status I added to the Protect check shows at the top of the output.
Change which check statuses print first in the Protect summary log.

protect-js-every-workflow-run-attempt-li.search: Links to GitHub Actions workflow runs in the Protect check output: .github/workflows/protect.js builds each run link as run.html_url plus /attempts/run_attempt with a ?pr=<pull request number> query, at two checks.push sites, one for the run-level status and one for the pending or failed branch. The two sites duplicate this URL template, so a change must be made in both places. A link without the ?pr= suffix is inconsistent with the other links in the same check output.

pt2-torch-version-gate-must-stay-in-sync.search: PyTorch pt2 model loading with pickle deserialization disabled in MLflow is guarded by the torch version floor in _validate_pt2_archive_is_pickle_free, which requires torch 2.10 or newer; the pickle-free models guide and the pt2 test skips must agree with that floor. Requests about which torch version is needed to load pt2 models, changing the minimum torch version, or updating the pickle-free models docs go through this gate. Lowering the floor would admit weights_only versions with known bypass or memory-corruption issues, and advertising an older torch in the docs misleads users whose pt2 loads then fail. The guard raises an error asking the user to upgrade torch or enable the pickle flag, and the unverifiable-torch test patches the version to 2.9.1 and expects the 'Upgrade to torch >= 2.10' message.

pyenv-clone-tag-and-expected-sha-in-setu.search: The pyenv version used by the setup-pyenv composite GitHub Action on Linux is pinned in .github/actions/setup-pyenv/action.yml in two places, the git clone tag and the expected_sha compared against git rev-parse HEAD, and setup-python pins the Python micro versions that pyenv must be able to build. Requests to upgrade pyenv in CI, or changes to Python versions used by model serving test environments, go through this action. Changing only one of the tag or the SHA makes the CI job fail early with a pyenv SHA mismatch error, and a mismatch is not retried, so model-serving environment setup never starts. pyproject-tool-mlflow-release-version-is.search: The mlflow release workflow's prod PyPI upload gate, labeled Validate ref and version, reads the [tool.mlflow-release] version marker in the root pyproject.toml, which is a major.minor release-branch marker and does not affect the built package version. The published version lives in mlflow/version.py, which setup.py reads, and setuptools ignores [tool.*] tables. Requests to fix a failing release to PyPI prod, change the version marker for a release branch, or add version metadata to pyproject.toml go through this marker. Adding a [project] version table instead conflicts with setup.py's dynamic version and the MLFLOW_SKINNY package-name switch. TestPyPI skips this gate, and whether dev/pyproject.py preserves this table when it regenerates the root file is not confirmed.

redact-credentials-from-tracking-uri-in-.search: Error and log messages that format a tracking or backend store URI in the mlflow-artifacts artifact repository, such as _validate_uri_scheme in mlflow_artifacts_repo.py used when the server runs with --serve-artifacts, must redact credentials before formatting. The tracing exporter can log a warning containing the full backend store URI, so a database URL with a user and password leaks the password in cleartext into server logs. Redaction should strip userinfo from the netloc and drop params, query and fragment while keeping scheme, host, port and path, because query strings can also carry secrets such as password or odbc_connect PWD values. The scheme check itself does not change, and URIs without credentials format the same as before.

Tracing exporter warning prints the tracking URI password in cleartext, how do I hide it?
mlflow-artifacts tracking URI error message leaks credentials, make it redact secrets
Keep tracking URI secrets out of error messages and logs in the artifact server

redis-budget-window-must-carry-and-match.search: The Redis-backed gateway budget tracker in mlflow/gateway/budget_tracker/redis.py enforces budget policies by creating a budget window in Redis through _ENSURE_WINDOW_LUA and rejecting requests in should_reject_request when spend exceeds the limit, returning HTTP 429. When a budget policy's duration is edited, for example from monthly to daily, the stored window must carry duration_unit and duration_value so the window rolls over when the applied policy differs, and windows whose duration does not match the local policy are skipped by _window_duration_matches. Without this, a process on an older policy version keeps a monthly window and users get 429 responses that cite a daily limit resetting a month away. Comparing window_start alone is insufficient because a daily and monthly window can start at the same instant.

release-build-must-explicitly-clear-mlfl.search: The legacy branch-2.11 release build in dev/build.py main chooses between the full mlflow wheel and the mlflow-skinny wheel by passing package-selecting environment variables to the setup.py child process. An ambient MLFLOW_SKINNY value in the CI or shell environment leaks into the build because the environment is merged before the extra variables, so a release run can publish mlflow-skinny instead of mlflow. The fix is to pass MLFLOW_SKINNY explicitly in every package-type branch, an empty string for release and 1 for skinny, so a stale value is never inherited. Any new package-selecting variable needs the same explicit treatment.

release-package-requires-the-pre-built-j.search: The branch-2.11 release packaging of the full mlflow wheel in dev/build.py main requires the prebuilt tracking server web UI in mlflow/server/js/build, which setup.py only bundles if the directory exists at build time. A release build that runs without the UI built first would ship a wheel missing or with a broken UI, so main checks JS_BUILD_DIR exists and is non-empty before the release build and exits with yarn build instructions otherwise. This guard applies only to the full release package, not the skinny package, and must run before any build call. If the UI build output location changes in setup.py or the JS build, JS_BUILD_DIR must change with it.

wait-for-async-test-conditions-by-bounde.search: Writing Python tests in this repository that wait for asynchronous work such as a server starting up or a background job finishing: the python-style skill guidance in .claude/skills/python-style/SKILL.md says to poll a condition against a time.monotonic deadline instead of a single time.sleep. The pattern is a deadline of about 30 seconds, a loop that checks the condition with a roughly 0.5 second sleep between tries, and a while/else that raises TimeoutError with a clear message. Fixed sleeps are flaky on slow CI and give no hint that the system was still starting, unless elapsed time is the behavior under test.

whitespace-check-diffs-the-local-git-che.search: The lint CI job's whitespace-only PR check in dev/check_whitespace_only.py no longer downloads the pull request diff from GitHub; get_pr_diff(base_revision) runs git diff between the base revision and HEAD in the local clone. The lint workflow in .github/workflows/lint.yml passes --base-revision HEAD^1, which exists only because the checkout uses fetch-depth 2, so lowering the fetch depth or removing the base fetch makes the git diff fail with a CalledProcessError and the lint step errors instead of checking the PR. The fetch depth in lint.yml and the --base-revision value must be changed together.
